articles.author: Chandelis Duster
articles.description: President Trump said there were "negative forces" predicting things that he says won't happen.
articles.title: Trump downplays calls for AI slowdown

articles.author: Kristin Wright
articles.description: Wisconsin Congressman Tom Tiffany escaped a sinking plane and swam to shallow water after an emergency landing in a lake. Tiffany and the pilot called 911 from on top of the plane.
articles.title: Wisconsin congressman survives emergency plane landing, swims to safety

articles.author: Kristin Wright
articles.description: Actor Tatyana Ali says her healing journey after a traumatic childbirth has inspired her advocacy for Black maternal health, including support for midwives, doulas and other birth workers.
articles.title: Actor Tatyana Ali is advocating for Black and Indigenous maternal health

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Indonesian rescuers said about 130 passengers and crew are missing after a ferry carrying more than 240 people sank in bad weather in the Java Sea on Sunday.
articles.title: Indonesian passenger ship overturns, sparking search for at least 129 missing

articles.author: Tom Bowman
articles.description: A young Canadian mother shares her memories of being an ISIS bride, and her harrowing escape from the extremist group.
articles.title: How a young woman was recruited to ISIS — and how she eventually escaped

articles.author: Chandelis Duster
articles.description: The Canadian singer opened up her 16-show residency in Paris at the Plenitude Arena. The entire series is sold out.
articles.title: Celine Dion returns to the stage after battling rare illness

articles.author: Ava Berger
articles.description: Nazira Haji Zada, a lawful permanent resident, conceded to being an "alien terrorist." It marks the first case in the Alien Terrorist Removal Court.
articles.title: Alien Terrorist Removal Court deports legal US resident to Afghanistan in first-ever case

articles.author: David Cox
articles.description: That's a quote from former rugby star Gareth Thomas, who is HIV positive. At the International AIDS Conference in Rio this year, he spoke out about the isolation and discrimination tied to the virus.
articles.title: 'People are still afraid of those three letters': Fighting the stigma of HIV

articles.author: Katheryn Houghton
articles.description: As state governments grapple with how to determine who's sick enough to be excused from new Medicaid work requirements, some families are already struggling with what illnesses guarantee health coverage because of a disability.
articles.title: A cancer survivor hoped to work — then she lost her Medicaid disability coverage

articles.author: Glen Weldon
articles.description: The Pitt, Hacks, Widow's Bay and Pluribus are leading the Emmy nominations pack this year. Here's who we'll have our fingers crossed for on Monday night.
articles.title: If the Emmys were up to us ...

articles.author: Krishani Dhanji
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Hanson’s comments on Albanese’s mother ‘gratuitous and unnecessary’: Hume
Jane Hume has joined the pile on, blasting Pauline Hanson for her comments about Anthony Albanese’s mother.
I think that these comments were gratuitous and unnecessary. And the idea that you would disparage people that have grown up in social housing, I think, is a little distasteful. I mean, it doubles down on the fact that Senator Hanson has also disrespected our veteran community with her atrocious comments about Andrew Hastie in that cartoon. Calling a veteran a traitor, I think, is possibly the worst thing you can do.
But this does seem to be a common theme in One Nation now, that sort of unnecessarily provocative rhetoric.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Politics live: Fugitive developer Jean Nassif tells Icac ‘I’m going to speak my heart’; Taylor dubs Labor’s social media reform a ‘big brother bill’

articles.author: Benita Kolovos and Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
Motorcycle club president Peter ‘Tiki’ Mason, 71, crashed and died on the Western Highway at Trawalla, west of Ballarat, on Sunday

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The death of a motorcyclist who reportedly hit a pothole has put the government under renewed pressure over the state of Victoria’s roads.
Emergency services were called to Trawalla, west of Ballarat, shortly before 1pm on Sunday after reports a motorcycle had struck a pothole. The 71-year-old rider, from Ballarat, died at the scene after reportedly losing control on the Western Highway, near Trawalla Road.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Motorcyclist’s ‘senseless’ death reignites debate over ‘pothole crisis’ in Victoria

articles.author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
articles.description:
Electoral Commission finds abuse, particularly of women, minority ethnic and disabled people, is affecting candidates’ behaviour
Abuse and intimidation of election candidates is “a serious and growing concern”, the Electoral Commission has said, as a review of this year’s local and mayoral elections in England revealed a surge in threats to those who stood.
More than half of the candidates for Labour or Reform UK reported abuse while those most likely to be targeted were women, people from minority ethnic backgrounds and those with disabilities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rise in abuse of election candidates is ‘changing politics’ in England

articles.author: Amanda Meade Media correspondent
articles.description:
Alleged victim tells court he froze and was ‘in disbelief’ after broadcaster kissed him on corner of his lips at public event
A prominent athlete froze and was “shocked and embarrassed” when Alan Jones kissed him on the side of his mouth at a public event, the broadcaster’s trial at Sydney’s Downing Centre has heard.
The witness said the kiss on the corner of his lips happened years after Jones sent him a weekly bouquet of flowers after he had complimented the flowers on Jones’s dining table. He said Jones’s driver would drop the flowers at his home every week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alan Jones told prominent athlete ‘I would like to be kissing you all night’ after alleged assault, trial hears

articles.author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
articles.description:
TGA issues alert after person was hospitalised after believing they were taking experimental weight loss drug retatrutide

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A patient who tore their oesophagus after taking a counterfeit version of an experimental weight loss drug has prompted Australia’s medicines regulator to warn of serious risks of such products.
The concern relates to retatrutide, a type of drug known as a peptide. Retatrutide has not been approved by the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) or regulators overseas, and it cannot be legally prescribed or sold in Australia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Peptide user tore oesophagus after using counterfeit product, Australian regulator warns

articles.author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
articles.description:
New immigration policy has attracted bipartisan condemnation, with Labor warning it would damage construction, healthcare and agriculture

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation says it will cut the number of temporary migrants in Australia by more than 750,000 over three years, targeting international students and family members of skilled migrants in a “net-negative” plan.
But the business and agriculture sectors have warned the plan would badly hurt the economy and weaken essential services, without lifting living standards for Australians.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: One Nation vows to cut migration by 750,000 amid warnings move would damage economy

articles.author: Sian Cain and agencies
articles.description:
Miki Zohar accuses Oscar-winning directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor of ‘treason against the state’

‘They know the house they are bombing is full of children’: NAZA’s directors on their devastating film about Israeli intelligence

Israel’s culture minister has called for the Oscar-winning Israeli directors of NAZA, a documentary about the country’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, to be stripped of their citizenship, accusing them of “treason against the state”.
NAZA, which was produced by the Guardian, is named for an acronym used by Israel’s intelligence service to indicate how many civilians it expects to die in an airstrike on Gaza.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israeli minister threatens to strip Israeli film-makers of citizenship over Gaza documentary NAZA

articles.author: Jakub Krupa in Stockholm
articles.description:
This live blog has now closed – you can read the latest news story here

If you’re looking just for a single story to quickly catch up on the story of tonight, let’s cross to our Nordic correspondent, Miranda Bryant, for her preview.
The prospect of far-right anti-immigration Sweden Democrats entering the government has understandably attracted a lot of international attention, particularly coming just days after the Alternative für Deutschland won the regional elections in Saxony Anhalt in Germany.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Centre-left bloc leads Swedish elections – as it happened

articles.author: Keely Aouga
articles.description:
Craig Berg was hypothermic but alert when located on Isle Royale by Michigan police and officials during solo hike
A 70-year-old hiker who had been missing for a week on a Michigan island was rescued on Saturday, according to the US Coast Guard.
Craig Berg was located on Isle Royale with the help of backpackers, Michigan state police troopers and local officials. Even though Berg was found injured and hypothermic, he is “alive and alert”, according to a statement posted to the Isle Royale national park’s Facebook page.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Missing US hiker, 70, found injured on remote island after week-long search

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Whist drive ticket embedded in rock and news article on Great Train Robbers among items discovered during 10-year restoration
Lost or long-discarded items revealing glimpses of the behind-the-scenes life of Buckingham Palace staff over decades have been uncovered during the restoration of the UK monarchy’s HQ.
Misplaced belongings, found beneath the floorboards, in other areas of the royal residence and preserved within the fabric of the building, include a ticket to a whist drive run by the royal household’s social club from nearly 80 years ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hidden history of royal staff uncovered in Buckingham Palace restoration

articles.author: Miranda Bryant Nordic correspondent
articles.description:
Race too close to call and may take days to become clear despite early exit polls suggesting left bloc win
With most of the votes counted, Sweden’s national election remained too close to call on Sunday night, with left-wing parties holding a lead of just a single seat according to a partial tally by the election authority.
Earlier in the night, exit polls suggested that the country was on course for a brand new left-leaning government. But as the votes were counted, it was apparent it could take days for the outcome to become clear.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Swedish election: centre-left parties lead by just a single seat with most votes counted

articles.author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
articles.description:
Kirsty McNeill reaffirms Labour’s 0.7% of GDP pledge and promises value for money to allay voter concerns
The development minister, Kirsty McNeill, has declared herself “a huge believer in aid”, as she reaffirmed Labour’s manifesto pledge to return to a target of 0.7% of national income spending.
McNeill, a former adviser to Gordon Brown and senior executive at Save the Children, declined to give any timetable, repeating the formula that the government would work towards the target “when fiscal circumstances allow”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Sweat the asset’: new development minister plots path to make UK aid count

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Prime minister vows to ‘reindustrialise Britain’ through new partnership with business 
The prime minister is to host business leaders, entrepreneurs and local mayors at Downing Street on Monday to pitch his government as a “partner for growth” that can offer a stable platform for investment and jobs in the UK.
Ahead of the event, Andy Burnham said the country had “everything it needs to succeed”, including talented people and world-class universities, but requires “a culture shift in how Britain does business” if it is to unlock its full potential.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham to host entrepreneurs and local mayors at No 10 on Monday

articles.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
articles.description:
US president brushes off Andy Burnham’s opposition to referendum and says he will remove Irish whiskey tariff 
Donald Trump has reiterated his support for Irish unification and brushed off Andy Burnham’s opposition to a referendum.
“Everybody says that. Then things happen,” the US president said on Sunday of the British prime minister’s response.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Donald Trump doubles down on support for united Ireland

articles.author: Keely Aouga
articles.description:
The 8ft statue, installed in Phoenix last week to mark one year since Kirk’s killing, was found painted red
A newly unveiled statue of the rightwing activist Charlie Kirk was vandalized at the Turning Point USA headquarters in Phoenix, Arizona.
The statue was found with red spray-paint. A nearby poster memorial in front of the statue was vandalized with red paint as well.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New Charlie Kirk statue vandalized at Turning Point USA headquarters

articles.author: Roque Planas
articles.description:
Police officer shared location of a woman with his relative who is accused of abusing woman
A San Jose police officer was fired for using his department’s Flock license plate tracking system to share the location of a woman with the suspect accused of abusing her, Chief Paul Joseph told NBC Bay Area on Friday.
The firing marks another in a growing number of cases of misuse of a controversial surveillance technology that has expanded rapidly over the last several years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: San Jose officer fired for misusing Flock camera database in domestic abuse case

articles.author: Keely Aouga
articles.description:
Disturbing and AI-generated versions of Dr Seuss character have been used to threaten schools and communities
Schools and law enforcement authorities in the US are issuing warnings against a viral “Cat in the Hat” social media trend in which disturbing or AI-generated versions of the Dr Seuss character are used to threaten students, schools and communities.
The latest warnings come as safety concerns increase and several teenagers have been arrested or charged over posts connected to the trend.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US schools and police warn about viral ‘Cat in the Hat’ trend after teens’ arrests

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
Vice-president wears religion on his sleeve but winding spiritual path could alienate evangelicals and Catholics
US vice-president JD Vance has worn his religion on his sleeve since converting to Catholicism in 2019. He recently published a book, Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith, and memorably met the late Pope Francis at the Vatican on Easter Sunday in 2025, a day before the pontiff died.
But his religious identity could take on new weight as he positions himself for a presidential run in 2028, in which a successful campaign would make him only the third Catholic president in US history. Vance’s winding spiritual path – combined with his avowed evangelical roots – have the potential to stymie him, as he seeks to retain the Christian nationalist voters that have sustained Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again (Maga) movement while wooing fellow Catholics.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: JD Vance’s Catholicism could be at odds with Maga evangelicals in 2028

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
PM has so far declined to insert curbs on UK-based donors, despite £72m donations from billionaires to Reform UK
Trade unions, MPs and donors have urged the government to look again at party funding rules, after Reform UK insisted £72m in donations from two crypto billionaires was within the law.
Andy Burnham, a previous backer of caps on domestic donations, has so far declined to insert any curbs in the elections bill that would apply to UK-based donors.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trade unions, MPs and donors urge Burnham to revisit party funding rules

articles.author: Amy Hawkins and Charlotte Higgins in Kyiv
articles.description:
Ukrainian Railways says former British PM and David Petraeus crossed into Poland shortly before drone attack near border
A train carrying Boris Johnson and the former CIA chief David Petraeus may have been the target of a Russian drone strike that hit a train engine near the Poland-Ukraine border, according to Ukrainian Railways.
Ukraine’s foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, described the attack as “Putin’s terror knocking directly on the doors of the EU and Nato”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Train carrying Boris Johnson and ex-CIA chief may have been targeted in Russian strike, officials say

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem and Seham Tantesh in Gaza
articles.description:
Woman’s family says she died of injuries after being shot in the head while sitting inside a tent near Khan Younis
A pregnant Palestinian woman died on Saturday from injuries sustained after being shot in the head by Israeli forces south of Khan Younis, according to her family and medical workers, as strikes across Gaza killed at least 10 people in 48 hours.
The woman, named as Iman Shalouf, 27, who was nearly eight months pregnant, was sitting inside her family’s tent in the al-Mawasi area when Israeli gunfire struck her, according to paramedics and witnesses.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pregnant woman among more than 10 killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza

articles.author: Jon Henley and agencies
articles.description:
Search and rescue agency says 107 people brought to safety from vessel hit by bad weather in Java Sea
Rescue workers in Indonesia said at least six people had died and 130 others were missing on Sunday after a ferry sailing between the islands of Java and Borneo capsized in bad weather.
Basarnas, Indonesia’s national search and rescue agency, said 107 people had been rescued from the Virgo ⁠Transport 8 vessel, which set sail on Saturday with 243 ​people onboard, including 30 crew members, ​from ‌the East Java ‌city of Surabaya.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At least six dead and 130 missing after Indonesian ferry capsizes, officials say

articles.author: Timothy Pratt
articles.description:
Key government meeting this month will consider US bid to try James ‘Fergie’ Chambers over alleged support for Hamas
Attorneys for James “Fergie” Chambers, the US citizen and wealthy donor to leftwing and humanitarian projects worldwide who is currently imprisoned in Madrid and sought in extradition, have submitted a brief ahead of a decisive government meeting on the case.
Meanwhile, Chambers’ partner, the actor and activist Stella Schnabel, met last week with multiple members of the Spanish parliament to assert his innocence.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pressure builds in Spain to deny US extradition request for leftwing donor

articles.author: Jon Henley and agencies
articles.description:
Iran-allied Houthis say drones and missiles used in attack that targeted ‘weapons depots and command and control centres’ in southern Saudi Arabia
Houthi fighters have said they used drones and missiles to attack a military base in southern Saudi Arabia, as Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government described the rebels’ swift advance along the Red Sea coast as a “painful” development in a new front in the Iran war.
The UN said on Sunday that nearly 86,000 people had fled Yemen, most of them since early September when the Iran-backed Houthi rebels launched a large-scale offensive that last week resulted in the capture of a key port city and an island on the Bab al-Mandab strait, a crucial shipping alternative to the strait of Hormuz.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Houthis claim attack on Saudi base as fighting flares with Yemeni forces

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Prime minister’s office tells families of those missing ‘the nation stands with you’ as search and rescue efforts continue
One person has died and more than 30 are missing after a ferry sank off the coast of Vanuatu, the country’s government says.
The vessel, MV Matui, had set sail with more than 40 passengers and crew on Friday from the island of Santo to Ambae island in very rough seas, but did not arrive.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: One dead and more than 30 missing after ferry sinks off Vanuatu coast in rough seas

articles.author: Oliver Holmes and agencies
articles.description:
Riyadh has increased use of East-West pipeline since start of war on Iran to bypass closure of strait of Hormuz
Saudi Arabia has shut down a critical oil pipeline, accusing militants in Iraq of launching drone attacks on the export route being used to bypass the lockdown of the strait of Hormuz.
The world’s largest ⁠crude oil exporter has increased its use of the 745-mile (1,200km) pipeline running across the Arabian peninsula, which links Abqaiq, near the Gulf, to the port of Yanbu, on the Red Sea, since the US-Israeli war against Iran began.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saudi Arabia shuts down key oil pipeline, blaming drones from Iraq

articles.author: Reuters in Kampala
articles.description:
Royal guards carry casket through streets of Fort Portal amid row over appointment of Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma
Uganda’s King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, long the world’s youngest monarch, has been buried among the tombs of his royal forebears as ⁠his Tooro kingdom looked to put ⁠a bitter succession battle behind ​it.
Oyo’s appointed successor, the news anchor Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, cast nine coffee berries into the grave at the Karambi Royal Tombs, marking the formal handover of power in the western Ugandan kingdom.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burial of King Oyo takes place in Uganda as news anchor prepares for throne

articles.author: Guardian staff and Associated Press
articles.description:
Alleged members of Black Axe criminal network that swindled US women out of $6m flown from South Africa
Six Nigerian nationals linked to an organized criminal network that allegedly swindled American women out of more than $6m through online romance scams were extradited to the United States on Friday.
South African police confirmed they were to be extradited earlier on Friday, while local news in Africa confirmed that the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, known as the Hawks, facilitated their handover to officials from the US Federal Bureau of Investigation and Secret Service at Cape Town international airport, in collaboration with Interpol South Africa.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Six Nigerians extradited to US over $6m online romance scam

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Incident is latest to raise questions over Israel’s ability or willingness to stop violent settlers in occupied territory
An Israeli soldier has shot a Palestinian man, wounding him in the leg, as settlers confronted villagers by grazing livestock on Palestinian-owned land in the town of Faqqua in the occupied West Bank.
Witnesses said a group of settlers had entered the area with their livestock, prompting residents to try to stop them. Israeli forces then intervened and, according to men at the scene, opened fire at residents. One of them shot Qassem Hussam, a Palestinian man in his mid-30s, wounding him in the leg.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: IDF soldier filmed shooting Palestinian in leg amid West Bank settler standoff

articles.author: Oliver Holmes
articles.description:
Chinese president’s arrival in Delhi seen as step towards reconciliation after deadly 2020 military clash
The Chinese president, Xi Jinping, has received a red-carpet welcome in India for a summit of Brics developing nations, as regional rivals Beijing and Delhi make a public display of thawing relations while quietly competing to lead at a time of shaky US global dominance.
As Xi stepped off the plane, he was walked past an honour guard of Indian soldiers and traditional dancers in colourful dresses. Later on Saturday, he was due to attend a gala dinner for the two-day summit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Xi Jinping gets red carpet at Brics summit amid thaw in India-China relations

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
The deadly fire had begun in the ferry’s cargo hold, then tore through the ship within seconds
The bodies of passengers killed in a ferry fire off the Philippines arrived at a port near the resort town of Coron, Palawan, on Saturday morning, as the country’s coast guard warned the death toll of 35 would grow.
Tents were being set up to receive 30 bodies brought from the M/V June Aster, which ran aground near the tourist hotspot after a fire erupted on Wednesday evening and tore through the vessel “in seconds”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Death toll from Philippines ferry fire rises to 35, as officials warn toll will grow

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The presidential briefing documents were declassified on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks
Several dozen presidential briefing documents declassified on Friday, the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, detail intelligence that government officials had gathered about Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida leading up to the hijackings that killed nearly 3,000 people and upended American national security.
The documents illustrate security analysts’ tracking of Bin Laden’s movements and support system, as well as concerns about possible threats to US targets. They also detail officials’ understanding of his network in the United States and other countries, including how his operations were financed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: CIA releases dozens of presidential daily briefs on Bin Laden and al-Qaida from before 9/11

articles.author: Agence France-Press in Bangkok
articles.description:
Phra Wachirayan Wi arrested alongside woman he was filmed having sex with in latest scandal to hit country’s clergy
Police in Thailand have arrested a senior Buddhist monk on suspicion of embezzling $2.8m intended for his monastery, alongside a suspected female accomplice he was filmed having sex with.
The case is the latest scandal to hit the clergy in the Buddhist-majority country, after a sex and extortion case involving senior monks last year prompted public outrage and calls for greater scrutiny of temple finances.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Buddhist monk arrested in Thailand on suspicion of embezzling $2.8m

articles.author: Karen McVeigh
articles.description:
Her Horizon Fund seeks $100m to stop practice harming 230m women and girls globally  
Frontline activists and leaders in the fight against female genital mutilation, which has affected more than 230 million women and girls worldwide, have welcomed an unprecedented $15.5m (£11.4m) fund aimed at creating “unstoppable momentum” to finally end the practice.
The launch of the fund comes as women’s rights are increasingly under attack and donor funding is in sharp decline, particularly for work led by FGM survivors in local communities. It is thought to be the largest single philanthropic contribution to ending the practice of FGM.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: $15m fund launched to create ‘unstoppable momentum’ to end FGM worldwide

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Canadian PM Mark Carney hosts president in Calgary, where he grew up alongside large Ukrainian community
Canada offered support on Thursday to boost Ukraine’s air defenses and help replenish its drone stocks, as the countries pledged to deepen their alliance during a visit by Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Mark Carney hosted the president of Ukraine in Calgary in the western province of Alberta, where the Canadian prime minister grew up among a large community of people with Ukrainian heritage.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada offers air defense support for Ukraine as Zelenskyy visits

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Family of late King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV reject committee’s choice of cousin and TV presenter as new monarch
A traditional Ugandan kingdom has become engulfed in a bitter succession dispute after the family of a king who recently died rejected the selection of a television news anchor as his successor.
King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who became the world’s youngest reigning monarch when he took the throne in the kingdom of Tooro in 1995 at the age of three, died on 27 August in the US, where he was receiving cancer treatment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Secret son revelation ignites bitter succession dispute in Ugandan kingdom

articles.author: Tora Agarwala
articles.description:
Following six years of talks, Pitt Rivers Museum will return body parts collected by British colonial administrators to north-east India
Anthropologists and community leaders from Nagaland, a remote state in north-eastern India bordering Myanmar, have expressed joy and relief that human remains belonging to their ancestors that had been on display in a British museum for nearly a century are finally being returned.
On Monday, the Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford announced that 39 pieces of human remains – including parts of skulls, a finger and a piece of skin with hair – belonging to the Naga tribes, will be returned to Nagaland after six years of negotiation between the community and the museum.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Our forefathers are coming back’: Naga people celebrate after Oxford museum agrees to return remains

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Rubio visits Ecuador and welcomes cooperation after campaign of unilateral strikes on alleged ‘narco-terrorists’
The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, gave new clarity on the approach toward combating drug trafficking in Latin American waters, saying the Trump administration was focused on working with allied countries and aligning with their laws but insisted the military would “still blow up ships if need be”.
The public acknowledgment of a shift in US strategy comes a year after Washington began a campaign of unilateral deadly strikes against those it calls “narco-terrorists” operating boats in international waters.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rubio signals shift to working with allies to fight drug trade as latest boat strike kills three

articles.author: Andrew Roth and agencies
articles.description:
Trump administration to seek extra funding from Congress to ‘dismantle’ Los Tiguerones over narcotics trafficking
The US has designated Ecuador’s Los Tiguerones gang, which stormed a television station during a live broadcast in 2024, as a terrorist organisation as the Trump administration expands its campaign against narcotics traffickers it says are destabilising Latin America.
The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, made the announcement in Quito, where he met Ecuadorian president Daniel Noboa, one of several rightwing allies of Donald Trump whom Rubio is courting as a security partner during a three-nation tour through Latin America that began on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Notorious Ecuadorian crime gang designated a terrorist group by US

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba announces decision to pull out in post on X, citing tensions over ‘Harry-Meghan nonsense’
Uganda is withdrawing from the Duke of Sussex’s Invictus Games, the country’s military chief has said, out of respect for King Charles amid division over the “Harry-Meghan nonsense”.
Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, son of the Ugandan president, made the surprise announcement in a post on X on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Uganda to withdraw from Invictus Games ‘out of respect for King Charles’, says military chief

articles.author: Natricia Duncan and agencies
articles.description:
Andrew Frederick’s body was found in property he was staying at in Grenada in January
The family of a British father who was found dead in the Caribbean in January is urging authorities in Grenada to work with UK police to uncover the truth about his death.
Andrew Frederick’s body was found in the property he was staying at in Grenada on 4 January. An autopsy, performed in the same week by a privately hired pathologist, concluded that the 47-year-old’s death was a homicide.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Family of British man found dead in Grenada ask local police to work with UK investigators

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Three men are on trial over the death of brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their friend, US citizen Jack Carter Rhoad, in Ensenada
The father of two Australian surfers killed in Mexico two years ago testified in court on Tuesday that his life had been turned into hell, as the high-profile trial continued into its second day.
Three men are charged in the killing of Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33, respectively, and their 30-year-old American friend Jack Carter Rhoad, who were on a surfing trip to Mexico’s Pacific coast in April 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s hell’: father of slain Australian surfers tells Mexico homicide trial about identifying sons’ bodies

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
India’s statistical system once commanded respect, and its data on economic and social indicators was considered rigorous – that appears to have eroded
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
There isn’t much that we Indians agree on these days. GDP numbers are no exception. Last week, India released glowing GDP numbers for the latest quarter – 7.8% growth – higher than the forecast 7%. It sparked a furore.
Subhash Garg, a former finance secretary under Narendra Modi’s government and now a critic, reframed what Modi called a “herculean feat” as mere smoke and mirrors. According to Garg, the government revised last year’s current-price GDP downwards to inflate this year’s number – he believes the real growth is only 2.6%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Trust deficit’: Why India’s economic data has sparked a furore

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Kathmandu
articles.description:
Foreign minister Shisir Khanal tells the Guardian the world’s biggest economies need to help Nepal, which contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions 
Nepal is demanding $20m in climate compensation for the recent devastating floods, as a senior minister called on the world’s most polluting countries to “wake up” and accept shared responsibility for a disaster that led to the death or disappearance of more than 6,000 people.
Scientists believe the climate crisis had a role to play in the floods, which were triggered when a melting glacier partially collapsed and set off a deadly landslide and flash flooding through Chinese-controlled Tibet and Nepal in late August. So far, more than 1,300 are confirmed dead and more than 5,500 still missing, with hopes of their survival diminished after 12 days of rescue operations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster

articles.author: William Christou
articles.description:
Chinese man at Trishuli hydropower project and Nepali woman in Nuwakot found 10 days into rescue operation
Emergency responders have rescued a Chinese man and a Nepali woman in two separate operations as authorities continued to search for thousands of people missing 10 days after massive floods hit Nepal.
The Nepali military said on Saturday a joint team comprising personnel from its army and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre (740ft) tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Pictures showed him being evacuated by helicopter after being carried out of the tunnel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flash flood disaster

articles.author: Oliver Wainwright
articles.description:
A bloated ballroom, a six-storey military HQ, a helipad-cum-cocktail patio, a gilded angel on a giant arch honouring himself … our architecture critic deplores the decorator-in-chief’s mutilation of Washington
When you have a developer as US president, you might expect some zhooshing up of the capital. A few buildings renovated, maybe some parks replanted. But when you have a megalomaniac builder in charge, things can get out of hand. A decade ago, when Donald Trump was first elected, I asked what it might mean for the US to be led by a real estate tycoon whose career had left a trail of broken promises, angry buyers and endless lawsuits, with rules flouted, heritage trampled and the world pockmarked by a fleet of aspirational towers clad with a flimsy veneer of luxury. The answer is worse than I could have imagined.
With the air of a nightmarish Hollywood sequel, Trump 2 has seen the president’s true architectural ambitions unleashed: The Blingpire Strikes Back. As America’s self-styled decorator-in-chief, Trump has not only overseen the gilded mutilation of the White House, but embarked on the Mar-a-Lagofication of Washington DC itself, applying his gold paintbrush to statuary, daubing ponds with flaking pool liner, and brewing plans for a colossal triumphal arch – all procured in a blizzard of no-bid contracts. And, in true dodgy salesman style, this programme of bauble-building is turning out to be a high-profile decoy for deeper damage being wrought elsewhere.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The desecration of DC: from a giant arch to a nuke-proof bunker, Trump’s legacy-building blingfest is an architectural atrocity

articles.author: Keely Aouga
articles.description:
The 8ft statue, installed in Phoenix last week to mark one year since Kirk’s killing, was found painted red
A newly unveiled statue of the rightwing activist Charlie Kirk was vandalized at the Turning Point USA headquarters in Phoenix, Arizona.
The statue was found with red spray-paint. A nearby poster memorial in front of the statue was vandalized with red paint as well.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New Charlie Kirk statue vandalized at Turning Point USA headquarters

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
Vice-president wears religion on his sleeve but winding spiritual path could alienate evangelicals and Catholics
US vice-president JD Vance has worn his religion on his sleeve since converting to Catholicism in 2019. He recently published a book, Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith, and memorably met the late Pope Francis at the Vatican on Easter Sunday in 2025, a day before the pontiff died.
But his religious identity could take on new weight as he positions himself for a presidential run in 2028, in which a successful campaign would make him only the third Catholic president in US history. Vance’s winding spiritual path – combined with his avowed evangelical roots – have the potential to stymie him, as he seeks to retain the Christian nationalist voters that have sustained Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again (Maga) movement while wooing fellow Catholics.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: JD Vance’s Catholicism could be at odds with Maga evangelicals in 2028

articles.author: Jessica Glenza
articles.description:
Jefferson county coroner says 40-year-old woman died on Saturday, while two infants died with disease in August
A coroner in Pennsylvania announced the death of a 40-year-old woman associated with the state’s ongoing measles outbreak. The death appears to mark the third in the US state’s ongoing outbreak.
Two previous deaths in the state were in infant children. In one case, the infant was born with a genetic defect that made her vulnerable to infection. The second infant child was infected with measles, and died of a ruptured spleen.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pennsylvania reports apparent third measles-related death amid outbreak

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
A recent consultation on corporate reporting prizes the interests of shareholders over society. It’s a step in the wrong direction
The question of what corporations are for is deeply political. In a 1970 article for the New York Times, Milton Friedman argued that the “social responsibility of business is to increase its profits”. The idea that CEOs should worry about providing good jobs was “pure and unadulterated socialism”, he wrote. Friedman and his fellow neoliberals saw companies as vehicles for enforcing their politics. Their ideas endured: UK bosses are now paid 130 times more than average workers.
Despite Andy Burnham’s pledge to end neoliberalism, a 12-week consultation recently launched by his government risks entrenching it. The consultation was first announced as part of the Starmer government’s crusade against “red tape”. The average annual report for some businesses now runs to 98,000 words, and no doubt there are areas that could be simplified. But the consultation proposes removing vital information and presumes that company reports primarily serve shareholders, rather than other stakeholders. Both are steps in the wrong direction.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on the government’s corporate reforms: entrenching neoliberalism, not ending it | Editorial

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany and pilot swim to safety after plane made emergency landing in lake
A Republican congressman said he had to swim to safety after a plane he was traveling in made an emergency landing in a lake late Saturday.
Representative Tom Tiffany says he was returning from the La Crosse county Lincoln Day Dinner when the light aircraft lost power as it approached Wausau downtown airport. The pilot made an emergency landing in Lake Wausau. They both ended up in the water and swam to safety.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Wisconsin congressman swims to safety after plane makes emergency landing in lake

articles.author: Dave Schilling
articles.description:
The government apparently has an issue with paths for cyclists. Take it from someone who can’t ride a bike: this makes no sense
I’m out of gas. Not metaphorically. Literally, my car has the barest minimum amount of fuel in it. This is not because I like to live dangerously, a la the great literary hero Austin Powers, but because gas is more expensive than ever. I have nowhere to be today, so I’m allowing my car to sit idle, empty and alone, lest my bank account disappear into the Phantom Zone of negative balance. If things get sticky, I can take public transit or, God forbid, ride a bike.
Except I can’t ride a bike, thanks to my parents, who were too busy doing more important tasks than teaching me, like arguing or falling asleep. But for many Americans, riding a bike is a perfectly normal thing to do. Am I humiliated that one of the many basic skills for life that I don’t know is considered so simple that it became a common idiom for something that’s easy? Yes, of course. I don’t live dangerously, I live humiliatingly. Humiliation is my middle name. Dave Humiliation Schilling. Go on, point and laugh at the photo of me in this article. Get it out of your system so we can move along.
Dave Schilling is a Los Angeles-based writer and humorist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why is the Trump administration calling bike lanes ‘DEI’? | Dave Schilling

articles.author: Anthony Scaramucci
articles.description:
Sacked after less than two weeks as Donald Trump’s communications director, the financier and podcaster reflects on the mistakes he made in an exclusive extract from his new book
• Plus: What it’s like to be fired by Trump, by four people who know
19 July 2017. My phone rings. White House operator: “Please hold for the president.”
I do. Of course.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The president doesn’t want you here any more’: Anthony Scaramucci on what really happened during the 11 days he worked in the White House

articles.author: Jeremy Barr in Washington
articles.description:
The former New York Times columnist is taking a step away from politics to focus on moral and humanistic concerns the media rarely cover
David Brooks knows there are plenty of podcasts out there. But as the veteran commentator prepares to launch his own, he believes there is still space for someone to tackle the big moral questions facing us all.
Brooks, who left the New York Times in February after 22 years and joined the Atlantic magazine full-time as a staff writer, hopes to fill that market gap with a new video podcast called The Permanent Questions, funded in part by Yale University, that will air weekly starting on Sunday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘There’s a weird market failure in media’: David Brooks on how his new podcast will tackle the big questions

articles.author: As told to Kate Lloyd, Julian Borger and David Smith
articles.description:
What’s it like to be shown the door by the US president? A former national security adviser, an Apprentice contestant and more share their stories
• Plus: The truth about my 11 days in the White House, by Anthony Scaramucci
Gene Folkes, 62, based in Manhattan, was a contestant on season 10 of The Apprentice, which aired in 2010. A former air force recruiter until 1991, he retrained as an investment banker, then launched his own business before appearing on the reality show. He was fired by Trump in episode 5. He now runs the technology consulting firm OshunX and hosts a podcast, Folkes Unfettered.
I didn’t audition to be on The Apprentice. I received the call out of the blue: “Would you be interested in doing this show?” I didn’t know a lot about it. However, like any young business person, you look for people who you consider titans. There’s this mythology around Trump. He was one of the people I wanted to emulate.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I said, if you want to fire me, just fire me. And so he did’: my showdown with Donald Trump

articles.author: David Smith in Dallas
articles.description:
President the star of the show at two-day convention, but party’s plan to treat November elections as referendum on Trump himself poses grave risks
“We’re going to have a good time listening to music,” Donald Trump told thousands of supporters in downtown Dallas before handing the mic to an opera singer, “because I’m getting a little bit tired of politics now.”
Millions of Americans seem tired of politics after a decade dominated by Trump. So the US president’s decision to close out this week’s first ever Republican midterm convention with a plea – treat November’s congressional elections as a referendum on Trump himself – was received by his Democratic opponents with glee.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump personality cult alive and well in Dallas – will it power Republican midterm success?

articles.author: Jameel Jaffer
articles.description:
Over the past quarter-century, the US supreme court has repeatedly failed to protect first amendment rights. We are suffering the consequences
Congress ratified the first amendment in 1791 but the supreme court didn’t breathe life into it until after the first world war, when prosecutions of antiwar protesters led the justices Oliver Wendell Holmes and Louis Brandeis – and then, fortunately, other justices as well – to realize that US democracy would be undermined, not strengthened, by allowing the government to suppress disfavored political opinions.
Repression during the cold war led the court to better protect the freedom of association, and government efforts to cover up official ineptitude and criminality during the Vietnam war spurred the court to better protect the freedom of the press. It took time, but in each of these instances the court responded to wartime repression by developing new legal doctrine that more robustly protected first amendment freedoms.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The ‘war on terror’ weakened the first amendment. Now we desperately need it | Jameel Jaffer

articles.author: Simon Jenkins
articles.description:
The US president is ever more wayward – and has little interest in defending Europe. The constitution may hold him to account, but we can’t wait
If Americans vote for a Republican majority in both houses of Congress in November, “I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000.” But they must not spend it in Canada or China or anywhere else outside the US. So said Donald Trump in Texas on Wednesday in advance of the forthcoming midterm elections. He further told voters to “Pretend that I’m on the ballot”. It was a climactic moment in an almost two-hour rant.
Trump does not have the required trillion dollars in his pocket, and it would be illegal to disperse such a sum without congressional approval. In any case, JD Vance now appears to have rowed back on the promise.
Simon Jenkins is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Wake up, Britain: Donald Trump’s US is no friend of ours. We must secure our own place in the world  | Simon Jenkins

Donald Trump has thrown a convention to amp up the Republican base ahead of the midterm elections, but not everyone is thrilled about it. Dozens of officials running for re-election have stayed away, choosing instead to campaign locally. Are they worried about Trump’s current unpopularity weighing down their ticket?

articles.title: Trump-a-palooza: why are Republicans avoiding the president? | Politics Weekly America

articles.description:
Charlie Kirk's death created a vacuum of power that still consumes the Maga right a year later. Immediately after Kirk was shot and killed, his ultraconservative activist organization Turning Point USA announced that his widow, Erika Kirk, would replace her late husband as CEO. But as Guardian reporter J Oliver Conroy tells Kai Wright, conspiracy theories pushed by Kirk's former allies and proteges have dogged both the organization and Erika Kirk herself. Real questions remain about whether Erika Kirk can maintain the enormous power and influence Turning Point holds on the right and what she is planning to do with the organization. Conroy spent months reporting on Charlie Kirk’s legacy talking to dozens of people within Turning Point USA and the larger Maga movement who view Charlie Kirk as a martyr. Conroy says martyrdom is a powerful force that can’t be controlled


J Oliver Conroy's Guardian story on Charlie Kirk and Turning Point USA:  Grief, fury, conspiracy: inside Turning Point USA after Charlie Kirk’s killing

articles.title: How Charlie Kirk's martyrdom fed the right. And then tore it apart – Stateside with Kai and Carter

US citizens will receive $5,000 if Republicans win midterms, Trump claims

Trump signs executive order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America

Abuse and intimidation of election candidates is “a serious and growing concern”, the Electoral Commission has said, as a review of this year’s local and mayoral elections in England revealed a surge in threats to those who stood.
More than half of the candidates for Labour or Reform UK reported abuse while those most likely to be targeted were women, people from minority ethnic backgrounds and those with disabilities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rise in abuse of election candidates is ‘changing politics’ in England

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Whist drive ticket embedded in rock and news article on Great Train Robbers among items discovered during 10-year restoration
Lost or long-discarded items revealing glimpses of the behind-the-scenes life of Buckingham Palace staff over decades have been uncovered during the restoration of the UK monarchy’s HQ.
Misplaced belongings, found beneath the floorboards, in other areas of the royal residence and preserved within the fabric of the building, include a ticket to a whist drive run by the royal household’s social club from nearly 80 years ago.

articles.title: Hidden history of royal staff uncovered in Buckingham Palace restoration

articles.author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
articles.description:
Kirsty McNeill reaffirms Labour’s 0.7% of GDP pledge and promises value for money to allay voter concerns
The development minister, Kirsty McNeill, has declared herself “a huge believer in aid”, as she reaffirmed Labour’s manifesto pledge to return to a target of 0.7% of national income spending.
McNeill, a former adviser to Gordon Brown and senior executive at Save the Children, declined to give any timetable, repeating the formula that the government would work towards the target “when fiscal circumstances allow”.

articles.title: ‘Sweat the asset’: new development minister plots path to make UK aid count

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Prime minister vows to ‘reindustrialise Britain’ through new partnership with business 
The prime minister is to host business leaders, entrepreneurs and local mayors at Downing Street on Monday to pitch his government as a “partner for growth” that can offer a stable platform for investment and jobs in the UK.
Ahead of the event, Andy Burnham said the country had “everything it needs to succeed”, including talented people and world-class universities, but requires “a culture shift in how Britain does business” if it is to unlock its full potential.

articles.title: Andy Burnham to host entrepreneurs and local mayors at No 10 on Monday

articles.description:
US president brushes off Andy Burnham’s opposition to referendum and says he will remove Irish whiskey tariff 
Donald Trump has reiterated his support for Irish unification and brushed off Andy Burnham’s opposition to a referendum.
“Everybody says that. Then things happen,” the US president said on Sunday of the British prime minister’s response.

articles.title: Donald Trump doubles down on support for united Ireland

PM has so far declined to insert curbs on UK-based donors, despite £72m donations from billionaires to Reform UK
Trade unions, MPs and donors have urged the government to look again at party funding rules, after Reform UK insisted £72m in donations from two crypto billionaires was within the law.

articles.title: Trade unions, MPs and donors urge Burnham to revisit party funding rules

articles.description:
Call for constitutional change in Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales likely to challenge Burnham’s devolution agenda
The first ministers of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland are to affirm their countries’ right to seek independence from the UK at a summit that is likely to challenge Andy Burnham’s devolution agenda.
The Plaid Cymru leader, Rhun ap Iorwerth, the Scottish National party leader, John Swinney, and the Sinn Féin vice-president, Michelle O’Neill, are expected to sign a memorandum of understanding at a landmark conference in Cardiff on Monday that will call on Westminster “to prepare, plan and facilitate constitutional change in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland”.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight force says it wants to speak to men in connection with anti-migrant unrest that left seven officers injured
Police have released images of six men they would like to speak to after violent disorder in Portsmouth last week that left seven officers injured.
About 200 people gathered at Eastney Marina on Sunday night after a small boat carrying asylum seekers arrived on the south coast having crossed the Channel. The activists dispersed the following day in the early hours.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police release images of six men sought after violent disorder in Portsmouth

Harborne and Delo’s cash could buy a massive head start in an election, but spending big has possible pitfalls 
Nigel Farage once said he could spend his £5m gift from Christopher Harborne on Ferraris if he wanted to, given its unconditional nature.
With the new donations to his party from Harborne and his fellow crypto billionaire Ben Delo of £72m over the past weekend alone, Farage’s party now has nearly enough cash to buy a Reform UK branded Ferrari for a party organiser in each of Britain’s 632 constituencies (though that would certainly be a waste and a bit of a tax headache).

articles.title: How could Reform UK spend its £72m of new billionaire donations?

articles.description:
Party’s economic spokesperson says donations are a ‘breakthrough moment’ as Labour’s Angela Rayner warns of possible retrospective action

Reform UK’s £72m donations may be caught by new bill, Rayner suggests

Christopher Harborne matches £36m Reform donation of Ben Delo

Analysis: Donations of £72m make Reform’s prospects both rosier and riskier

A charity in Powys provides the land while growers do the hard work, producing bumper crops for city children
Kilos and kilos of courgettes, cucumbers, tomatoes and salad leaves are ripe and ready for picking on a small Welsh farm in the rural county of Powys.
The haul being harvested by Tilly Gomersall is not just impressive after a difficult growing season hit by a record string of heatwaves and drought across all of Wales and most of England, but all the more remarkable given that 18 months ago the site was uncultivated pasture.

articles.title: A joyful harvest: the young Welsh farmers growing food for Birmingham

Fire survivors and bereaved urge Barnet Group to ‘reconsider’ appointment of Laura Johnson, who pushed for cheaper contractor
Grenfell survivors and bereaved relatives have criticised the “outrageous decision” to hire a director who oversaw cost-cutting at Grenfell Tower in a £150,000-a-year senior council housing role.
Laura Johnson, the director of housing at the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (RBKC) at the time of the 2017 Grenfell fire, has been appointed the permanent director of development and property at the Barnet Group, which manages the borough’s 13,000 council homes.

articles.title: Director who oversaw Grenfell cost-cutting given senior council housing role

articles.author: Heather Stewart Economics editor

Iran war and turbulent global bond markets add to pressure as rate decisions loom this week in major western economies

Economics viewpoint: perilous UK economic conditions trace back to Trump

Central bankers in economies including the US, Japan and the UK will face a moment of truth this week, as surging inflation raises the prospect of higher interest rates.
Policymakers in all three countries will set rates in the next seven days against the backdrop of turbulent global bond markets.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Surging inflation puts interest rates back in focus as policymakers meet in Japan, US and UK

Minister says manifesto pledge is not being dropped but focus is now on building council houses

UK politics live – latest updates

The government is unlikely to meet its target of building 1.5m homes in England, Angela Rayner has acknowledged, saying there was only a “slim chance” enough houses would be built before the next election.
The manifesto pledge to build 1.5m houses by the next election was a “stretch target”, the communities secretary added, but said it was not being ditched and she was “definitely not giving up”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Only slim chance target of 1.5m new homes in England will be met, Angela Rayner says

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor

Authorities were caught off guard by the disruption, which they labelled a ‘protest’ despite mass intimidation tactics
To anybody watching the videos of a group of masked men, all wearing black, descending on the port of Dover last weekend, it was immediately obvious that something novel and disturbing was happening: a mass intimidation in uniform not seen in Britain since the 1930s.
Yet to the police and the rest of the UK’s intelligence apparatus, the arrival of the men chanting “stop the boats” was a surprise, despite the fact that residents of a village 18 miles away tried to report that dozens of men were congregating there on the Friday, threatening to go to Dover and “attack Muslims”.

articles.title: Dover unrest exposes serious flaws in Britain’s handling of far-right extremism

articles.description:
Ex-Tory chancellor says economy has ‘fallen off a cliff’ since Brexit but rejoining union could be ‘quite simple’
The former chancellor George Osborne said Britain’s economy had “fallen off a cliff” since Brexit and that rejoining the European Union’s customs union would be the fastest route to recovery.

articles.title: Unpaid carers could die before seeing justice for overpayments scandal, charities warn

articles.author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
articles.description:
Pilot project in Preston comes with apprenticeship offer for Neets at end of three-week course
In a youth centre opposite Preston bus station, the UK government is trying to address two of the greatest challenges facing the national economy: AI and youth unemployment.
The hope is that one will solve – rather than cause – the other. In a room at the recently opened Vault, a community hub in the Lancashire city, an “AI bootcamp” is under way – part of a trial in the north-west to give 16- to 24-year-olds AI training.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Really helpful’: the AI bootcamps aimed at addressing UK youth unemployment

articles.description:
Thousands of miles of new power lines are needed to deliver climate targets and energy security, but bills will rise in the short term and opponents are mobilising 
Britain is embarking on one of the largest overhauls of its electricity grid in generations – a megaproject in which five times more infrastructure will be built by 2030 than was constructed during the previous three decades.
Tens of billions of pounds are being spent on new pylons, subsea cables and converter stations to connect a growing fleet of wind and solar farms and carry clean power to where it is needed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mapped: the £150bn megaproject that aims to protect Britain from energy shocks

articles.description:
Criticism of three-year threshold repayment freeze in England prompts update to guidance warning terms and conditions could change
University students taking out student loans in England are to be warned that the terms and conditions could change so they are better informed about what they are signing up to, the government has said.

 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK government to offer clearer guidance on student loans after repayment row

Under a heavy police presence, approximately 400 protesters marched into the centre of town for a second weekend, chanting slogans hostile to migrants. Donald Trump says he would ‘love’ to see united Ireland
